newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-MUSTER AND CORRETJA BEATEN IN GENERALI OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER AND CORRETJA BEATEN IN GENERALI OPEN.

text.p: Thomas Muster and Alex Corretja suffered reverses on their favourite clay surface on Thursday when they were ousted in the third round of the Generali Open.
Top seed Muster, the clay-court king when he had a long series of wins in 1995 including the French Open title, was beaten on Austrian home soil by Czech Slava Dosedel 2-6 6-3 6-4.
Third seed Corretja, ranked fourth in the world following excellent performances this year, lost to unfancied Spanish compatriot Galo Blanco 7-6 (7-4) 7-5.
Second seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov's match against Italian Renzo Furlan was interrupted by rain and its conclusion postponed to Friday. The Russian won the first set 7-6 but trailed 4-5 in the second.
Kafelnikov is the only survivor among the top five seeds. Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten and Spain's Alberto Berasategui, seeded fourth and fifth, were defeated in the second round on Wednesday.
Corretja appeared still weary after winning in Stuttgart last Sunday for his third tournament victory of the year.

Muster, ranked fifth in the world, said he had particularly struggled with Dosedel's returns. The loss was especially bitter as it ended his clay-court season with a disappointing nine wins in 18 matches.
The Austrian's biggest clay success of the year was reaching the quarter-finals in St Poelten in mid-May. However, he won two hard-court tournaments in Dubai and Key Biscayne earlier in the year.
"I have no problems playing on clay. It is still my favourite surface," Muster said. "My problem at the moment is that I can't take my chances.
"I feel physically fit, even now after three sets. I just need more match practice and I have concentration problems."
Muster will play only on hard courts for the rest of the year. He next competes in Montreal and Cincinatti to prepare for the U.S. Open.
